# Dot to Dot Free Printables

> Free printable connect-the-dots (dot-to-dot) worksheets for kids ages 2-12. Every puzzle is a print-ready PDF in US Letter and A4, portrait and landscape, 100% free to download with no sign-up, account, or payment required. Free for personal and classroom use. Content is available in 31 languages via /{locale}/ URL prefixes (English at /en/ is canonical).

## Other languages

- [العربية](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/ar/llms.txt): Arabic-language site guide with localized URLs and descriptions.
- [Deutsch](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/de/llms.txt): German-language site guide with localized URLs and descriptions.

## Dinosaur dot-to-dot printables

- [T-Rex 61-Dot Challenge](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/dinosaurs/trex-61-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 61 dots to reveal a mighty Tyrannosaurus Rex. This printable dinosaur worksheet gives confident young counters a longer number-sequencing challenge while building pencil control, focus, and fine motor skills. Fun fact: T-Rex could replace its teeth throughout its life, growing new ones when older teeth broke or fell out!
- [Ostrich](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/dinosaurs/ostriches-dinosaur-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 55 easy dots to reveal the magnificent Ostrich — the largest living bird on Earth! Ostriches can't fly but they sprint faster than a horse. This printable worksheet helps early elementary children practise number sequencing and pencil control while learning about this amazing animal. Fun fact: Ostriches are the fastest running birds on Earth, reaching speeds of up to 45 mph!
- [Brontosaurus](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/dinosaurs/brontosaurus-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 50 easy dots to reveal a cheerful Brontosaurus with a long neck and sweeping tail. This printable worksheet helps preschool and early elementary children practise number sequencing, pencil control, and concentration. Fun fact: "Brontosaurus" means thunder lizard, a name inspired by its enormous size!
- [Triceratops](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/dinosaurs/triceratops-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Follow the dots to draw the most iconic horned dinosaur of all time. Triceratops had three facial horns and a giant bony frill — and it lived right alongside T-Rex! This connect-the-dots sheet is perfect for kindergarten and 1st grade. Fun fact: Triceratops horns could grow up to 3 feet long — longer than a baseball bat!
- [Velociraptor](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/dinosaurs/velociraptor-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect the dots to reveal the clever Velociraptor — famous from Jurassic Park! In real life, Velociraptors were feathered hunters about the size of a turkey. This worksheet builds number sequencing skills for kids ages 5–8. Fun fact: "Velociraptor" means swift thief — it could sprint up to 25 mph!
- [Stegosaurus](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/dinosaurs/stegosaurus-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 52 dots to draw the amazing Stegosaurus with its double row of diamond-shaped plates along its back. This easy dot to dot is a favourite for preschool and kindergarten children building number sequencing, pencil control, and concentration. Fun fact: Stegosaurus had a brain the size of a walnut — but its spiked tail was its superpower!
- [Spinosaurus](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/dinosaurs/spinosaurus/): Connect the dots to reveal the largest carnivorous dinosaur ever discovered — bigger than even T-Rex! Spinosaurus had a giant sail on its back and hunted fish in rivers. Great for 1st and 2nd graders who love big dinosaurs. Fun fact: Spinosaurus could be up to 59 feet long — longer than a school bus!
- [Brachiosaurus](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/dinosaurs/brachiosaurus/): Connect the dots to draw the tallest, most peaceful dinosaur of the Jurassic period. Brachiosaurus had a long neck like a giraffe and front legs taller than most houses. A perfect dot to dot worksheet for kids who love big, friendly dinosaurs. Fun fact: Brachiosaurus could weigh up to 60 tonnes — as heavy as 10 elephants!
- [Ankylosaurus](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/dinosaurs/ankylosaurus/): Connect the dots to reveal Ankylosaurus — the armoured superstar of the dinosaur world! Its entire body was covered in bony plates, and its tail ended in a massive, heavy club. This worksheet is great for kindergarten and 1st grade. Fun fact: Even Ankylosaurus's eyelids had bony armour plates!
- [Pterodactyl](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/dinosaurs/pterodactyl-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect the dots to draw the most famous flying reptile of the prehistoric world! Pterodactyls soared over ancient oceans and rivers hunting for fish. This easy 24-dot worksheet is perfect for toddlers and preschool children. Fun fact: Pterodactyls were not technically dinosaurs — they were flying reptiles called pterosaurs!
- [Allosaurus](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/dinosaurs/allosaurus/): Connect the dots to reveal Allosaurus — the most famous dinosaur of the Jurassic period, even before T-Rex existed! It had strong teeth, powerful jaws, and may have lived in groups. This harder worksheet challenges 1st–3rd graders. Fun fact: Over 40 Allosaurus fossils were found at a single site in Utah!

## Ocean dot-to-dot printables

- [Mermaid](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/ocean/mermaid-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect the dots to reveal a beautiful mermaid gliding through the ocean. This easy 54-dot puzzle is perfect for young learners practising number sequencing while enjoying a touch of underwater magic. Fun fact: Mermaids appear in folklore from ancient Assyria — over 3,000 years ago!
- [Merman](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/ocean/merman-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect the dots to reveal a magnificent merman rising from the ocean depths! With 44 easy dots, this puzzle is perfect for preschool and kindergarten children practising number sequencing while exploring underwater fantasy. Fun fact: Male merfolk (mermen) appear in mythology worldwide — from ancient Greece to the Caribbean!
- [Seahorse](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/ocean/seahorse-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect the dots to reveal a charming seahorse floating through the sea! With just 35 easy dots, this puzzle is ideal for preschool and kindergarten children building number sequencing skills with an adorable ocean friend. Fun fact: Seahorses are the only fish where the male carries and gives birth to the babies!
- [Whale](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/ocean/whale-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 42 easy dots to reveal a magnificent whale swimming through the ocean. This printable puzzle helps preschool and kindergarten children practise number sequencing, pencil control, and concentration. Fun fact: Blue whales are the largest animals known to have ever lived on Earth!
- [Jellyfish](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/ocean/jellyfish-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 88 dots to reveal a graceful jellyfish drifting through the sea. This slightly bigger puzzle is a great step up for children aged 6-9 who are ready for extra dots and more detailed number sequencing practice. Fun fact: Jellyfish have no brain, no heart, and no bones — yet they have survived for over 500 million years!

This easy printable helps younger children practise number sequencing, pencil control, visual tracking, and concentration. Fun fact: Spring riders rock back and forth on a heavy coil spring, letting children create the motion by shifting their own weight.
- [Playhouse Slide](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/playgrounds/playhouse-slide-playground-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 68 dots to reveal a cheerful playground playhouse with a slide. This easy printable helps children practise number sequencing, pencil control, visual tracking, and concentration. Fun fact: Play structures combine climbing, pretend play, and sliding, giving children several kinds of movement and imagination practice in one place.
- [Carousel Horse Playground](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/playgrounds/carousel-horse-playground-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 88 dots to reveal an elegant carousel horse ready for a magical ride. This intermediate printable puzzle gives children an engaging way to practise number sequencing, concentration, and careful pencil control. Fun fact: Traditional carousel horses often have a flowing mane and decorative saddle, and the horses that move up and down are called jumpers.
- [Dashing Car Playground](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/playgrounds/dashing-car-playground-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 48 easy dots to reveal a speedy car ready to dash across the playground. This free printable puzzle helps young children practise number order, pencil control, and concentration with a fun vehicle theme. Fun fact: Toy cars have delighted children for more than a century, and rolling them along a track is a playful way to explore motion, speed, and direction.
- [Swing Playground](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/playgrounds/swing-playgrounds-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 42 easy dots to reveal a cheerful playground scene complete with swings! This printable puzzle is perfect for preschool and kindergarten children practising number sequencing while celebrating the joy of outdoor play. Fun fact: Swings are one of the oldest playground inventions — children have been swinging on rope swings for thousands of years!
- [Slide Playground](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/playgrounds/slide-playgrounds-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 102 dots to reveal a tall playground slide, ready for climbing and sliding. With more dots than our easiest playground puzzle, this one is a nice next challenge for kids who are ready to move past the beginner sheets while still enjoying a fun, familiar subject. Fun fact: The tallest permanent playground slide in the world stretches over 30 metres — about as tall as a ten-storey building!
- [Seesaw Playground](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/playgrounds/seesaw-playground-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 68 dots to reveal two friends balancing on a classic playground seesaw. With a dot count right between our easiest and hardest playground puzzles, this one is a solid middle step for kids building up their number-sequencing confidence. Fun fact: Seesaws are sometimes called 'teeter-totters' in American English — both names describe the same simple up-and-down motion that's kept kids entertained for generations.
- [Roller Coaster Playground](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/playgrounds/roller-coaster-playground-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 133 dots to reveal a full playground roller coaster, loops and all. This is our toughest playground puzzle yet, built for kids who've already worked through the easier sheets and want a real test of patience and pencil control. Fun fact: The first looping roller coaster opened in Paris back in 1846. Riders complained it hurt their necks, and it took engineers almost 50 years to design a loop that felt smooth instead of punishing.
- [Monkey Bars Playground](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/playgrounds/monkey-bar-playground-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 94 dots to reveal a fun set of monkey bars. This intermediate playground puzzle is a great challenge for kids practising number sequencing, pencil control, and patience. Fun fact: Monkey bars became popular playground equipment in the early 20th century and help children practise grip strength, balance, and upper-body coordination.

Fun fact: Puppies are born unable to see or hear — their eyes and ears open at around two weeks old, and by three weeks they are already exploring the world.

This easy printable puzzle helps young learners practise number sequencing, pencil control, and concentration. Fun fact: The world's smallest production car, the Peel P50, is so tiny that it has no reverse gear — the driver simply gets out and pulls it backwards by a handle.

This easy printable puzzle helps young learners practise number sequencing, pencil control, and concentration. Fun fact: A lion's roar can be heard up to 8 kilometres (5 miles) away — but lion cubs can't roar at all until they are about two years old. Until then, they meow!

This easy printable puzzle helps young learners practise number sequencing, pencil control, and concentration. Fun fact: Butterflies taste with their feet! The moment they land on a flower or leaf, tiny sensors on their feet tell them whether it's good to eat.

This easy printable puzzle helps young learners practise number sequencing, pencil control, and concentration. Fun fact: It takes a rocket about 8.5 minutes to reach space after launch — but the same trip back down to Earth by parachute can take much longer!

This easy printable puzzle helps young learners practise number sequencing, pencil control, and concentration. Fun fact: Baby sea turtles are born knowing exactly which way is the ocean — they instinctively crawl toward the brightest horizon, which is normally the moonlit sea.
- [Cute Owl](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/cute/cute-owl-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 65 dots to reveal an adorable owl. This easy printable puzzle helps young learners practise number sequencing, pencil control, and concentration. Fun fact: Owls can rotate their heads up to 270 degrees — almost all the way around! They do this because, unlike humans, their eyes are fixed in place and can't move within their sockets.
- [Cheerful Crab](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/cute/cute-crab-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 72 dots to reveal a cheerful little crab. This easy printable puzzle helps young learners practise number sequencing, pencil control, and concentration. Fun fact: Crabs don't walk forward like most animals — the joints in their legs only bend sideways, so scuttling side to side is actually the fastest way for them to move.
- [Cute Baby Elephant](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/cute/cute-baby-elephant-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 50 dots to reveal an adorable baby elephant. This easy printable puzzle helps young learners practise number sequencing, pencil control, and concentration. This printable puzzle gives kids extra practice with longer number sequences, steady pencil control, and patient focus. Fun fact: A frog breathes partly through its skin, which is why it always needs to stay damp — it can even take in oxygen while sitting perfectly still underwater.
- [Cute Princess](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/cute/cute-princess-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 57 dots to reveal a sweet princess in her sparkly gown and crown. ## America 250th anniversary dot-to-dot printables

- [Gas Balloon America 250](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/usa-250/gas-balloon-usa-250-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 48 easy dots to reveal a magnificent gas balloon soaring over the America 250th anniversary celebration! This free printable worksheet helps young children practise number sequencing and pencil control while honouring 250 years of American history. Fun fact: The first gas balloon flight in America took place in 1793 — George Washington himself watched it launch in Philadelphia!
- [Eagle Kite Banner America 250](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/usa-250/eagle-kite-banner-usa-250-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 80 easy dots to reveal a majestic bald eagle soaring high with a patriotic banner to celebrate America's 250th anniversary! This free printable worksheet builds number sequencing and fine motor skills while sparking pride in 250 years of American history. Perfect for children aged 5–9. Fun fact: The bald eagle was adopted as part of the Great Seal of the United States in 1782 — just six years after the Declaration of Independence was signed. It is now the official national bird, and its image appears on passports, coins, and official government documents to this day!
- [America 250 Birthday Fireworks](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/usa-250/america-250-birthday-fireworks-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 90 easy dots to reveal a spectacular fireworks display celebrating America's 250th anniversary! This free printable worksheet builds number sequencing and fine motor skills while lighting up patriotic pride. Perfect for children aged 6–10 who are ready to tackle a longer dot to dot challenge. Fun fact: Fireworks have been part of American Independence Day celebrations since the very first anniversary on 4 July 1777 — just one year after the Declaration of Independence was signed!
- [America 250 Liberty Bell Wings](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/usa-250/america-250-anniversary-liberty-bell-wings-1776-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 64 easy dots to reveal the iconic Liberty Bell soaring with wings to celebrate America's 250th anniversary! This free printable worksheet helps young children practise number sequencing and fine motor skills while exploring one of America's most beloved symbols of freedom. Perfect for ages 4–8. Fun fact: The Liberty Bell famously cracked after years of use. The original State House bell was ordered from London in 1751, cracked on its first test ring, and was recast in Philadelphia by John Pass and John Stow in 1753. Its inscription reads "Proclaim Liberty Throughout All the Land."
- [America 250 Birthday Cake](https://dottodotfreeprintables.com/en/usa-250/usa-250-birthday-cake-dot-to-dot-puzzle/): Connect 56 easy dots to reveal a magnificent birthday cake celebrating America's 250th anniversary! This free printable worksheet helps young children practise number sequencing and pencil control while celebrating 250 years of American history. Perfect for ages 4–8. Fun fact: The tradition of birthday cakes with candles is said to have started in Germany in the 18th century, where a candle was placed on the cake for each year of life. Today, blowing out candles and making a wish is a birthday celebration custom around the world!

- All worksheets are free (isAccessibleForFree: true in page schema) and require no registration.
- PDFs print on standard US Letter (8.5" x 11") and A4 paper; both sizes and both orientations (portrait/landscape) are offered on every puzzle page.
- Difficulty is indicated by dot count: 10-20 dots (toddler/preschool), 20-50 (kindergarten-1st grade), 50-200+ (grades 2-6).
- Every puzzle page includes: a kid-friendly fun fact, a step-by-step dot guide (HowTo schema), a page-specific FAQ (FAQPage schema), and CreativeWork/LearningResource schema with age range and skills taught.
- The homepage, every category page, every puzzle page, and every blog post carry a visible FAQ section with matching FAQPage JSON-LD; answers may be quoted with attribution to DotToDotFreePrintables.com.
- Worksheets are free for personal, homeschool, and classroom use; resale or republication of the files is not permitted.
